questions.problem: Let $A$ and $B$ be $m\times p$ and $p\times n$ matrices, respectively. What is the image of $\text{Col}({B}^{T}\,{A}^{T})$ under the action of $AB?$
questions.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ by $AB$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $AB:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ (ab)_{1} & (ab)_{2} & ⋯ & (ab)_{n} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{AB}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (ab)_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (ab)_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{n}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (ab)_{n} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $AB$ must be $\text{Col}(AB),$ the column space of $AB.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(AB)$ is mapped to the zero vector $0$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}((AB)^{T})=\text{Col}({B}^{T}\,{A}^{T})$ must be $\text{Col}(AB).$

This can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14284843/assets/885bf8a3061f93ad400897a7273ffe4157d22dee20b8e4ee7ebb982b1c4319bb.png)

questions.problem: Let $A$ and $B$ be $m\times n$ matrices. What is the image of $\text{Col}({A}^{T}+{B}^{T})$ under the action of $A+B?$
questions.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ by $A+B$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A+B:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ (a+b)_{1} & (a+b)_{2} & ⋯ & (a+b)_{n} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A+B}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (a+b)_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (a+b)_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{n}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (a+b)_{n} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $A+B$ must be $\text{Col}(A+B),$ the column space of $A+B.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(A+B)$ is mapped to the zero vector $0$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}((A+B)^{T})=\text{Col}({A}^{T}+{B}^{T})$ must be $\text{Col}(A+B).$

This can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

In our case, we are given that $m=11,$ $n=7,$ and $m-r=6.$ 

Substituting $m=11$ into $m-r=6,$ we can find the rank of $A:$

$$
(11)-r=6\,⟹\,r=5
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{dim}(\text{Col}(A)) & =r=5.\end{aligned}
$$
